sections.h2: What is the fastest way to sell a house in Ramsey, MN?
sections.html:
The fastest route is a direct sale to a buyer who accepts the house in its present state, because it skips showings, repair negotiations and a lender's appraisal. A listing with an agent takes longer but reaches the widest group of buyers, and a sale you run yourself sits between the two.

Ramsey is a suburb in Anoka County about 22 miles north-northwest of downtown Minneapolis. U.S. Highways 10 and 169, which share a roadway here, and State Highway 47 are its main routes. The city covers 28.85 square miles of land, and much of it is less dense than the inner suburbs, with about 958 people per square mile. Many Ramsey houses are not on city sewer, and the city says about 4,200 private septic systems operate within its limits. That matters at sale time, as a later section explains.

  • Direct sale: no repairs asked of you, a closing date you set, and a price that reflects the work.
  • Agent listing: more exposure, plus preparation, showings and the buyer's financing timeline.
  • Selling alone: you save the commission and handle every form and negotiation yourself.

sections.h2: What do the Census Bureau figures say about Ramsey homeowners?
sections.html:
Ramsey is growing and family-heavy. Census figures put Ramsey at 29,624 residents in mid-2025, a rise of 7.2% over the April 2020 base of 27,636, and the city had 27,646 people in the 2020 count.

About 85% of homes are lived in by their owners, and the typical household has 2.66 people. Owners put the middle home's value at $359,600 for 2020 to 2024, while median gross rent is $1,826. Median household income is $116,415, and the average commute to work is 28.2 minutes. About 26% of residents are under 18. Some 92% of residents stayed in the same house for a full year.

If your Ramsey house has a big lot, a finished lower level or a three-car garage, put those points first in your listing or your pitch to a direct buyer.

sections.h2: Does Ramsey require a septic inspection before I sell?
sections.html:
Yes, if the house is on a private septic system. Ramsey City Code section 113-23 requires a compliance inspection on any sale or transfer of property served by an individual sewage treatment system. The city administers Minnesota Rules Chapter 7080 and says about 4,200 of these systems operate within its limits.

  • An MPCA-certified inspector must perform the inspection and report on the state's approved form. City inspectors cannot do it.
  • You give the buyer a Certificate of Compliance at or before closing, and a copy of the inspection goes to the city's Building Division within 15 days.
  • If the sale falls between November 1 and April 30 and the inspection cannot be completed, the seller and buyer may agree in writing that it will be finished by the following June 1.
  • A system that fails normally has to be brought into compliance within 12 months.

The winter window is open right now, so a seller listing in mid-November can still close with a spring inspection plan. Recent pumping does not replace the inspection, since pumping only addresses the tank and the inspector examines the entire system, including the drainfield. Each sale needs a new inspection even if you had one last year. Ask the Building Division at 763-433-9850 for the point-of-sale handout.

Owners of these systems also check for leaks and measure sludge and scum accumulations at least once every three years, and the city requires a septic pumping permit each time a tank is pumped. Keeping those permits and pumping records in a folder gives the inspector and the buyer a clear history of the system.

sections.h2: What should I know if my Ramsey house is a rental?
sections.html:
All residential rental properties in Ramsey must be licensed every year. Single-family rentals are inspected every three years, and multi-family buildings every year, against the 2021 International Property Maintenance Code, the city's rental code and its zoning code.

An inspection takes between 15 minutes and an hour. The inspector checks heating, plumbing and electrical systems, doors and windows, and exterior upkeep such as mowing, debris and vehicle licensing. A property that fails gets a correction list, and the license fee covers one follow-up visit. A third visit on the same issue can cost a $150 reinspection fee.

Two exceptions come up in sales. A house rented to a relative needs no license if it qualifies for Relative Homesteading with the Anoka County Assessor and you have applied for it. A contract for deed avoids licensing only if it is recorded with Anoka County and requires real principal payments, because an interest-only contract is treated as a rental. If you are selling with a tenant in place, give the buyer the latest inspection report and the license dates.

City utility accounts are another loose end. A tenant may hold the account in a tenant's name, but the property owner stays responsible for any unpaid balance, and bills arrive quarterly. Bring the account current before closing, and call Utility Billing at 763-576-4343 if you need to add a second name or fix the billing address.

sections.h2: Which Anoka County charges apply when a Ramsey deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Anoka County's Land Records office records the deed. Its fee schedule, effective July 1, 2025, lists the following charges that apply to a typical sale.

Anoka County recording charges for a house sale (fees effective July 1, 2025)
ItemCharge
Recording fee for a deed (abstract)$46.00
Conservation fee$5.00
State deed taxNet consideration x 0.0033
Deed tax when consideration is $3,000 or less$1.65
Well certificate$54.00
Attested copy$2.00

The county also asks for a completed electronic certificate of real estate value, an eCRV number on the deed and a "send tax statements to" line naming the buyer. Any delinquent taxes have to be cleared before a transfer, and a split of a tax parcel requires current-year taxes to be paid. Instead of the $54 well certificate, a deed may carry the statement that the seller does not know of any wells on the property. Minnesota Statutes section 103I.235 sets that rule, and section 513.55 requires your written disclosure to the buyer before the purchase agreement is signed.

sections.h2: Where did Ramsey come from, and who serves its schools?
sections.html:
Thomas Holmes and James Beatty built the Old Log Trading Post here in 1849, and Itasca Village was platted in 1852 with the first post office in Anoka County. The area became a township, was renamed Dover and then Ramsey, and the city incorporated on November 12, 1974 with about 8,000 people. Ramsey borders Andover, Anoka, Nowthen, Oak Grove, Dayton and Elk River.

Two school districts serve the city, Elk River and Anoka-Hennepin, and PACT Charter School operates inside Ramsey. Confirm which district applies to your address before you print a school name in an advertisement.

faqs.q: Do I need a septic inspection if I sell my Ramsey house in winter?
faqs.a: Yes, but the timing can shift. For sales between November 1 and April 30, the seller and buyer can close and agree that the inspection will be completed by the following June 1, if the inspection cannot be completed.

faqs.q: Who can perform a Ramsey point-of-sale septic inspection?
faqs.a: Only an MPCA-licensed septic inspector. City inspectors do not perform these inspections, and the seller gives the buyer the Certificate of Compliance at or before closing.

faqs.q: Does a contract for deed make my Ramsey property a rental?
faqs.a: It can. If the contract is recorded with Anoka County and sets reasonable principal payments, the city does not require a rental license. An unrecorded or interest-only contract is treated as a rental.

faqs.q: What are the recording charges for a Ramsey deed?
faqs.a: Anoka County charges $46 to record a deed and $5 as a conservation fee, plus state deed tax of the net price times 0.0033. A well certificate costs $54 unless the deed carries the no-wells statement.
The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 29,624, a gain of 7.2% over the April 2020 base. The 2020 census counted 27,646.
